newsitem.title: USA: Manpower up on encouraging European news - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Manpower up on encouraging European news - analysts.

text.p: Manpower Inc stock was up more than five points, boosted by positive news on its revenue growth in France, analysts said.
But analysts cautioned that the company benefitted from subsidies given by the French government to French companies last year to curb unemployment.

Manpower officials were not too positive about prospects for continued subsidies during a conference call following its earnings report Thursday, Jeff Silber, an analyst at Gerard Klauer Mattison & Co Inc, said.
"There are no guarantees," he said. "The French government tries these things on an experimental basis."
Manpower officials were not immediately available for comment.
About one-third of the company's revenues come from France, one analyst said.

"There was good news on the conference call about revenue growth in France and (Manpower) expects that strength to accelerate in 1997," H. Perry Boyle, an analyst at Alex. Brown said. The company's business in France represents about one-third of its revenue base, an analyst said.
"I'm urging caution," Boyle said. "(Manpower's) growth in France benefitted from French government subsidies in 1996 that may not be there in 1997."
Manpower stock was trading up 5-1/8 Thursday afternoon at 35-1/8 on higher-than-average volume of about 769,000 shares.

William Sutherland, an analyst at Janney Montgomery Scott agreed. "It's safer to assume they won't be there (in 1997)," he said. "The tax credit is used as a motivator for employers (in France) to hire and the (French government) will probably continue them, but not at levels seen in 1996."

Earlier Thursday, the Milwaukee-based temporary staffing services company reported sales of $2.0 billion in the fourth quarter ended December 31, up from $1.7 billion one year ago. Net income reached $48.1 million compared to $36.6 million in the corresponding period in 1995.

"The trend in France got stronger in January, so 1997 is off to a strong start," Sutherland said."That's important for the stock since it fell short of original expectations in the first half of 1996," he said.
"Manpower has gained back everything it lost in the past week," Boyle said. "There was nervousness about the fourth quarter, especially about the French business."
